draft.title: Sovereignty and enforcement
card: Sovereignty means a state has supreme authority over its own territory and people. Other states and international bodies cannot simply override its decisions.
There is no world government or police force to make a state obey human rights standards. This makes enforcement hard when a state will not comply.
Pressure can still come from outside. The UN can criticise a state or review its record, and other states can use diplomacy or sanctions.
Non-government organisations (NGOs), such as Amnesty International, and the media expose abuses and shape public opinion. This pressure may persuade a state to change, but it does not force it to.
draft.remember: Sovereignty limits enforcement, so human rights depend on pressure from the UN, states, NGOs and the media.

a.q: Why is it hard to enforce human rights against a state that refuses to comply?
opts: The state has supreme authority over its own territory
The state has not yet been told which rights apply
The UN has no interest in the rights of that state's people
NGOs and the media are banned from reporting abuses
a.why: Sovereignty gives a state supreme authority within its territory, and no world government can override it. The UN does take an interest in human rights, so the claim that it has none is wrong.
a.clue: Think about who has final authority inside a country.

b.q: A state is accused of jailing critics. An NGO publishes a report and newspapers abroad cover it. Which statement best describes what this pressure can do?
opts: It may persuade the state to change but cannot compel it
It compels the state to release the prisoners at once
It has no effect, as the state is free to ignore it
It replaces the need for the state's own laws on rights
b.why: NGOs and the media expose abuses and shape opinion, which may lead a state to change. They have no power to compel a sovereign state, so the claim that it forces release is wrong.
b.clue: NGOs and the media have influence but no police force.

a.best: The state has supreme authority over its own territory

b.best: It may persuade the state to change but cannot compel it

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may ... but cannot'). The other three are absolute claims, so a student can pick it from its form alone. The clue ('influence but no police force') also nearly states the answer.

opts: It can persuade the state, but it cannot force a change

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'No body can compel a sovereign state'. That is too absolute: the UN Security Council can make binding decisions under Chapter VII, including sanctions and authorising force. The card is more careful ('cannot simply override'), so the why should say pressure does not usually force a change, not that nothing ever can.
